claims.claim: Adapton separates tracked invalidation from demand-driven repair and proves incremental results correspond to from-scratch evaluation under its modeled semantics.

Nominal Adapton uses first-class names to control correspondence across runs; stable names permit reuse even when associated contents change, with dirtying/change propagation retaining responsibility for validity.
Ambiguous name reuse is a correctness problem; Nominal Adapton dynamically detects it, while follow-up precise-name/Fungi work moves uniqueness obligations into type-and-effect systems.
Current selected Aeneas has declaration-local structure but constructs fresh whole-crate contexts and exposes no public cross-request edit/invalidation protocol.
Anneal should separate logical subject identity, snapshot/generation identity, equality/fingerprints, and dependency/freshness evidence.
depends_on: nominal correspondence is distinct from repair
external stages may have dependencies not captured by a stable subject ID

claims.claim: Fine-grained dependency traces should be retained only when dependencies are conservatively observable and workload savings justify retention/invalidation complexity; otherwise recompute a coarse stage.

non_claims: No claim that Anneal should implement Adapton or Fungi.
No benchmark-derived threshold for dependency-graph retention.
No claim that content hashes cover hidden semantic inputs.
No claim that current Aeneas declaration IDs are stable or sufficient cache keys across snapshots.
